questions.prompt: Before relying on “Graph breaks”, what should a learner verify?
options: Use the held-out test split repeatedly to tune the model and report that score as unbiased.
Skip recording package versions because they cannot affect API or device behavior.
reuse identical inputs and settings, include warm-up/repeats, synchronize accelerators, and verify outputs as well as timing.
Assume all tensor dimensions and devices are interchangeable without checking them.
questions.answer_key: reuse identical inputs and settings, include warm-up/repeats, synchronize accelerators, and verify outputs as well as timing.
questions.explanation: This lesson recommends the following check: reuse identical inputs and settings, include warm-up/repeats, synchronize accelerators, and verify outputs as well as timing.

questions.prompt: Which pitfall matters when applying “Guards and recompilation”?
options: Catch every exception and silently replace failed results with zeros.
Do not publish a performance claim from one unsynchronized timing sample or a different workload.
Change several unrelated settings at once and infer which change fixed the result.
Treat successful imports as proof that the full model and evaluation pipeline are correct.
questions.answer_key: Do not publish a performance claim from one unsynchronized timing sample or a different workload.
questions.explanation: This topic-specific caution is important: Do not publish a performance claim from one unsynchronized timing sample or a different workload.
